title: Cartesia's New AI Architecture Cuts LLM Training Compute and Data Needs by 10x
summary:
Cartesia researchers have released an updated version of their Hierarchical Networks, or H-Nets, which allows large language models to learn from raw bytes rather than using standard fixed-chunk tokenization. The new architecture matches the performance of an open-source model trained on 11T tokens while requiring roughly 10x less computation and data. In separate controlled scaling experiments, the team reported efficiency gains of 3-5x over existing methods.

The work is the result of two years of research, following an initial H-Net preprint published in July 2025. By moving tokenization inside the model, H-Nets can dynamically chunk data, a process that Cartesia says improves scaling on coding data and variable names compared to Byte Pair Encoding. The company aims to apply this end-to-end optimization to diverse multimodal data to increase model intelligence.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Our new version finds up to 3-5x efficiency gains in controlled scaling law experiments, and at larger scale matches an open-source model trained on 11T tokens with ~10x less data and compute.
selectedTweets.text:
I've always believed that intelligence should come from simple, general building blocks that learn their own abstractions directly from raw data; in other words, the bitter lesson. I think we're finally seeing a real step towards AI that can learn from all data.

Language modeling on raw bytes is a microcosm of this ideal, and to me it's a central problem in AI: if we can't build LLMs that learn end-to-end from bytes, how will we handle the rest of the world's data that we understand even less?

Last year we introduced hierarchical networks (H-Nets) as a first step. Our new version finds up to 3-5x efficiency gains in controlled scaling law experiments, and at larger scale matches an open-source model trained on 11T tokens with ~10x less data and compute. The posts below walk through what we found and why we think it works.

selectedTweets.text:
We’ve seen incredible results in applying new ideas that bring tokenization into the main model, a culmination of 2 years of research — up to 10x compute and data gains on language models that we’ve trained!

What’s most exciting is that these hierarchical networks open up a new design space for building models that can be optimized end to end on raw data, something we don’t yet do very much of in AI.

This work is particularly exciting for us @cartesia, and a core part of our long term research agenda in building models that are fundamentally more intelligent at understanding diverse and multimodal data.
